 Delhi man arrested for allegedly spreading misinformation about fish deaths in Yamuna
 The arrest came two days after videos purportedly showing several dead fish floating in the river were shared on social media.

 Arun Sankar/AFP
 The Delhi Police has arrested a man for allegedly spreading misinformation about the deaths of several fish in the Yamuna near Sonia Vihar, PTI reported on Saturday.
 The arrest came two days after videos purportedly showing several dead fish floating in the river were shared on social media. The cause of the deaths has not been established.
 The accused, identified as Surender, had uploaded a video on social media on Thursday that purportedly showed the Wazirabad Water Treatment Plant. The video was widely shared amid concerns over the reported fish deaths, PTI reported.
 Surender was arrested following a first information report filed by the Delhi government’s irrigation and flood control department.
 He was booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to public mischief, making statements intended to cause public mischief and giving false information.
 He was later released on bail from the police station.
 Edited by Tanya Shrivastava.
